system_instruction:
You write a short evidence brief on the lung cancer care pathway for one Finnish wellbeing services county, for the county's health managers. You may use ONLY the claims provided. Each claim has an ID, a status and a text.

Rules:
1. Every sentence must list the IDs of the claims it relies on in claim_ids (at least one). Use IDs exactly as given. Do not cite anything that is not in the list.
2. Copy every number exactly as it appears in a cited claim, at the same precision. Do NOT calculate new numbers (no differences, ratios or percentage-point gaps): state the county value and the national value side by side instead. Spell out no numbers in words.
3. State uncertainty. Give 95% confidence intervals where the claim has one. Never say "certain": say the 95% confidence interval excludes (or includes) the national value. Say that the county shares are crude. They have two separate limitations: (a) they are not age-adjusted (if you say where age-adjusted values exist, cite claim fig:age_adjusted_only_kuva16); (b) they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients. Never present missing stage as the reason the shares are not age-adjusted. Where an age-adjusted value exists (Kuva 16, digitised from a figure, about ±0.5 percentage points), use it to say whether a gap holds after age adjustment, say it is digitised, and pass on any caveat in the claim's notes (e.g. a confidence interval that could not be read).
4. The treatment categories overlap (a patient can have several); never add them up or present them as a breakdown, and whenever a sentence mentions two or more county treatment shares, say in that sentence that the categories overlap. "No treatment record within 12 months" mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded; never call it "untreated" or "missing data". MDT records measure recording practice, not care.
5. Read the no-treatment-record share as a data-quality signal, using its 95% interval (the claim says "below", "above" or "not distinguishable" vs national). Only if the county's claim says "below" (the interval is entirely below national) may you say this is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, as an inference, not a finding; a low curative share is then less likely to be only a recording artefact. If it says "not distinguishable", say nothing about recording completeness. If it says "above", you may say low treatment shares may partly reflect unrecorded treatment.
6. Label status in the sentence itself: a sentence citing a claim with status "preliminary" must say "preliminary" (e.g. "preliminary, unpublished figures"); one citing "mentor insight" must say "mentor insight". Claims "verified by Hellu" were read in full by a teammate in documents we do not hold locally (regional pathway documents, the Health Care Act, THL guidance, a journal article); describe them by what they are, not as regional documents unless they are. Every sentence that cites a county share (a claim whose ID starts with "cty:") must say the share is crude (the word "crude"). A sentence citing a claim with status "recommendation (ours)" must say it is the team's recommendation (e.g. "the team recommends"). In what_to_do_first, cite the relevant team recommendation (rec:1, rec:2 or rec:3) together with the evidence claims that support it; do not add steps that are in neither.
7. Respect each claim's scope ("scope: …" in its notes). Never use a claim for something outside its scope: e.g. the HILMO ~90% claim concerns diagnosis concordance only and says nothing about treatment recording; a regional finding describes only the named region's document; national averages are not county figures.
8. Describe planned national measures as plans, with the plan's own verb and date, in the present tense: e.g. "the roadmap plans national pathways with target access times for five cancers by 2026–2028"; "the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation" (say "carried out", never "completed" or "implemented"). Attribute each plan to the document, measure and date in its notes ("plan: …"): the STM roadmap and the Filha programme are different documents with different dates; never mix them in one attribution. Never write "will" about national measures. Never use the words certain, proves, guarantees or definitely.
9. Each section has a headline (the main point, one sentence of at most 30 words, with claim IDs) and 2–4 detail sentences. "where_we_lag": where this county's pathway lags national values. "how_sure_are_we": what is well supported, what is uncertain and what public data cannot show. "what_to_do_first": the first steps, drawn from the team's draft recommendations and suited to this county's data, each backed by evidence claims.
10. Plain, direct English. No claims about other counties. No headings or numbering inside sentences. Apply these rules and the claim notes by writing accurately; do not restate them in the brief (do not write things like "this describes only its own document" or explain the meaning of a Finnish verb), and keep each sentence under about 60 words.

details.text: In Länsi-Uusimaa, the crude life-prolonging treatment share is 25.2% (95% CI 22.7–27.9; n=267/1058), with a 95% confidence interval that excludes and lies below the national 30.4% (4522/14873), while across overlapping treatment categories (where a patient can have several) the crude curative share of 31.9% (95% CI 29.1–34.7; n=337/1058) excludes and exceeds the national 27.0% (4009/14873).

Across these overlapping treatment categories (a patient can have several), the crude symptomatic treatment share is 40.1% (95% CI 37.2–43.1; n=424/1058), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 39.5% (5871/14873), and the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 28.5% (95% CI 25.9–31.3; n=302/1058), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 27.5% (4089/14873).

An MDT meeting is recorded for a crude share of 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7; n=2/1058) of patients, whose 95% confidence interval excludes and lies below the national 6.0% (893/14873), though MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures specialist procedures only from direct patient contacts.

Public registry data do not report county waiting times, but preliminary, unpublished national figures show lung cancer takes 155 days on average from symptoms to first treatment in Finland (versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark), comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care, the longest stage.

headline.text: Public registry data show diagnosis patterns, but crude county treatment shares lack age and stage adjustment, and public data omit primary care, referral, and treatment timestamps.

details.text: Taulukko 11 gives crude county shares that are not age-adjusted (county age-adjusted shares appear only in Kuva 16, with digitised national curative lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women, ±0.5 percentage points, and no digitised Länsi-Uusimaa value); as a separate limitation, shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types (diagnosis concordance only), while the crude 28.5% (95% CI 25.9–31.3; n=302/1058) with no treatment record within 12 months (95% CI includes the national 27.5%, 4089/14873) mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded, and Finland has no cancer quality registry.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned at all, and imaging appears only indirectly because diagnosis relies on clinical examination alone, such as imaging, in approximately 20% of patients.

For specialist care, public data show whether a lung cancer specialist visit appears in HILMO within 12 months (93.6% nationally) and which treatment type is recorded within 12 months, but cannot show when the first specialist visit or treatment started, and no reviewed regional pathway document reports whether stated target times are met.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions with handover alerts, and standardising referrals and diagnostic-phase contacts.

details.text: Because Länsi-Uusimaa's crude recorded MDT share is 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7; n=2/1058) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and crude life-prolonging share is 25.2% (95% CI 22.7–27.9; n=267/1058) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) across overlapping categories, with stage missing for about 48% nationally, the team recommends publishing per-county stage, drug, and MDT recording coverage as data-quality signals first.

Since Health Care Act §52 sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and preliminary national intervals average 41 days in primary care and 58 days in specialist care, the team recommends reporting access times (referral to first specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start) using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers.

Because a mentor insight notes weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings, and in reviewed regional pathway documents only KYS provides a referral template and a rule to refer persistent symptoms despite a clear X-ray while no reviewed document names a diagnostic contact, the team recommends adopting a KYS-style template, a persistent-symptoms rule, and a named diagnostic contact.

The team recommends acting while national plans proceed: STM roadmap measure 1.2.3 plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 (county adoption by 2029–2031) and measure 3.2.1 plans updating the quality registry decree by 2026–2028, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with primary-care referral criteria and time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.
